qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Permitted limestone quarries, kilns, and US river distribution terminals create local geographic entry barriers due to high weight-to-value transport economics, but bulk cement is a cyclical, energy-intensive commodity lacking sustained through-cycle pricing power above inflation.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12% across full cycle & lack of steady pricing power, REJECT). Permitted kilns and US river terminals confer strong local scale, but bulk cement remains a cyclical, carbon-intensive commodity with 10-year average ROCE below 10% and heavy EU ETS decarbonisation capex burdens.
qualitative.evidence: Full-cycle ROCE across 2015-2024 averaged ~9.5% (2015-2018 ranged 4.5-9.0%, rising above 12% only during the exceptional 2023-2024 post-COVID inflationary price spike). Free cash flow conversion is depressed at 59.3% due to high ongoing maintenance and environmental capex. The business lacks unilateral through-cycle pricing power against structural energy and carbon costs.
